review: 4:1–4:4 כִּי עַזָּה כַמָּוֶת … לֹא נָהָר יְכַבֶּנָּה / וְלֹא רַבִּים מַיִם — Song of Songs 8:6–7 word for word; the Arabic فَهُوَ كَالْمَوْتِ قَوِيّ / نَارُهُ لَظَى الْإِلٰه / لَا بِسَيْلٍ يَنْطَفِي / أَوْ بِكَثْرَةِ الْمِيَاه is that passage, and the Hebrew keeps the Song's own nouns.

2:1–2:2 עָרַבְתָּ בַּעֲדֵנוּ — the Arabic نُبْتَ عَنَّا is 'You stood surety for us'; עָרַב is the biblical verb of pledging (Gen 43:9; Prov 11:15), which is exactly the commercial image the Arabic uses, and it keeps the line from becoming a general 'You took our place'.

3:3–3:4 וְאֵימַת הַצְּלָב לֹא / חָסַם הָאַהֲבָה — the Arabic لَمْ يَكُنْ هَوْلُ الصَّلِيب / دُونَ ذَا الْحُبِّ يَحُول is 'the cross's horror could not bar that love'; חָסַם ('to muzzle, block') is used in the biblical sense of stopping a way (Ps 58:5 of the deaf adder), so the barrier is real but ineffective.

5:3–5:4 כָּל־מַחְשְׁבוֹת אֱנוֹשׁ / בָּהּ תִּשְׁתּוֹמֵם — the Arabic كُلُّ فِكْرٍ لِلْوَرَى / عِنْدَ ذَا الْحُبِّ يَحَار repeats 'all minds marvel' from stanza 3; the Hebrew keeps the repetition with the same verb (שָׁתַם → הִשְׁתּוֹמֵם), as the Arabic does.

1:3–1:4 נָשָׂאתָ בַבָּשָׂר / עֲוֺנֵנוּ וְדִינֵנוּ — the Arabic قَدْ حَمَلْتَ فِي الْجَسَد / إِثْمَنَا وَحُكْمَنَا pairs sin and sentence; the Hebrew keeps both, because the stanza goes on to distinguish the sentence from the guilt in stanza 3 of hymn 164.
